searchText: I'm bringing up the issue with mainnet/ testnet derivation. I'm suggesting deriving testnet as m/12381/3599/... mainnet m/12381/3600/.. As we move closer to mainnet it becomes more important Ideas? comments? I wouldn't want keys holding real funds and test funds shouldn't come from the same seed, there's too much chance to muck something up. We should have enough methods in place to separate out keys for different networks (different wallet names, different paths, _etc._) Not sure that this would bring anything more in terms of security, and it would lead to additional complexity throughout the tooling. <@!636950487089938462> Are you referring to BIP-43 derivation paths or some new derivation path? Using different seeds could work but it still need different derivation paths to eliminate issues around that > <@!636950487089938462> Are you referring to BIP-43 derivation paths or some new derivation path? <@301186049323958275> Yeah just for eth2 not eth1 Why do you need different derivation paths if you he different seeds? Because you will still derive mainnet keys regardless of where you put the seed. In eth1 it’s the same seed but different paths, it’s convenient and prevents mistakes (like sending mainnet tokens to testnet address) I'm unaware of there being different paths for mainnet and testnets, I thought they were all coin type 60.

excerpts.author: alon.ssv.network
excerpts.content:
I'm bringing up  the issue with mainnet/ testnet derivation. 
I'm suggesting deriving testnet as m/12381/3599/... 
mainnet m/12381/3600/.. 

As we move closer to mainnet it becomes more important
Ideas? comments?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
I wouldn't want keys holding real funds and test funds shouldn't come from the same seed, there's too much chance to muck something up.

We should have enough methods in place to separate out keys for different networks (different wallet names, different paths, _etc._)  Not sure that this would bring anything more in terms of security, and it would lead to additional complexity throughout the tooling.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: <@!636950487089938462> Are you referring to BIP-43 derivation paths or some new derivation path?

excerpts.author: alon.ssv.network
excerpts.content: Using different seeds could work but it still need different derivation paths to eliminate issues around that

excerpts.author: alon.ssv.network
excerpts.content:
Because you will still derive mainnet keys regardless of where you put the seed. 

In eth1 it’s the same seed but different paths, it’s convenient and prevents mistakes (like sending mainnet tokens to testnet address)
